title: Path Sum IV
summary: Given an ascending array of three-digit integers representing a binary tree with a depth less than 5, calculate the sum of all paths from the root to the leaves.
statement: Given an ascending array of three-digit integers representing a binary tree with a depth less than 5, calculate the sum of all paths from the root to the leaves. Each integer's digits represent the depth, position, and value of a node. Ensure the array forms a valid connected binary tree.
constraints: 1 <= len(nums) <= 15; each three-digit value encodes depth, position, and node value.
The encodings form a valid binary tree of depth at most four; sum every root-to-leaf path total.
hints: The hundreds and tens digits identify a node’s depth and position.
Store encoded positions in a map and recurse only into positions that exist.
Carry the running sum; at a node with no encoded children, contribute that sum.
Every leaf contributes exactly one root-to-leaf total, and shared ancestors are correctly included in each descendant leaf’s path.
editorial: Every leaf contributes exactly one root-to-leaf total, and shared ancestors are correctly included in each descendant leaf’s path.

tests.explanation: The paths 3→5 and 3→1 total eight and four, giving twelve.
The only root-to-leaf path totals four.
